 Andre the Giant left WWE legend ‘covered in blood’ during freak accident inside the ring
 November 18, 2026 by James Sweetnam 
 EXCLUSIVE: Andre the Giant accidentally left a wrestling legend with a nasty injury during a memorable moment. 
 During his career, the Frenchman solidified his status as one of the best competitors to have ever set foot inside the ring.
 Andre the Giant left Hacksaw Jim Duggan covered in blood
 On April 2, 1988, Hacksaw Jim Duggan knocked out Andre the Giant during an episode of WWF Superstars, in a twist that sent shockwaves through the wrestling industry.
 However, before the American landed his famous blow, he was handed a nasty injury by his rival.
 WOW: AJ Styles reveals the one regret he has from his match with The Undertaker at WWE WrestleMania 36 
 In an exclusive interview with Sporf via BetVictor Online Casino , Duggan reminisced: “If there was a giant in our business, Yokozuna , Umaga , The Big Show , Andre the Giant, it was ‘Duggan, get your 2×4’; I had to wrestle every giant there was. 
 “I ran down; I had my chin on Andre’s belly, I’m looking up at him like, ‘I’m not afraid of you’. He went to grab me, and his thumb hit my lip, and my lip fell down, and blood came pouring down my chest. It actually worked out great, everyone was like, ‘Where did the blood come from’? He beat me up with his thumb. WWF went off the air with me standing over Andre the Giant, covered in blood.”
 Hacksaw Jim Duggan on the origins of his wrestling rivalry with Andre the Giant
 Long before Hacksaw Jim Duggan and Andre the Giant faced off in WWF, the pair battled it out in Hawaii, with the New Yorker opening up about the fascinating details about how his first encounter with the all-time great came about.
 He explained: “I broke into wrestling in Texas with Fritz Von Erich, but I went up to New York for the WWF. After wrestling Hulk Hogan and Sergeant Slaughter, Vince McMahon Sr. called me into his office, and he was like, ‘Kid, you might have a future, but come up with something better than ‘Big Jim’ and get rid of that gold bath robe; we’re going to send you out to learn how to wrestle. We’re going to send you to Hawaii’.
 “I was a young guy, and they flew me to Hawaii, where I worked for ‘High Chief’ Peter Maivia . Of course, I’m young, and I’m wrestling all these grown men. My good friend, Haku (Meng), was over there, and we were making about $40 per week. The Chinese restaurant banned us from the all-you-can-eat buffet.
 “Anyway, they put me under a mask and called me, ‘The Convict’. Andre, on his way back from Japan, stopped in Hawaii, and he was the man who tore my mask off. Of course, everybody was like, ‘Who’s this guy’? But the bottom line is that I formed a great relationship with Andre as a young man. Years later, when I came into the WWF, I’m working with Andre; he allows me to knock him out with my 2×4. That elevated me from a mid-card guy to a main event guy. If Andre didn’t want to do that, he would’ve eaten my 2×4. 
 “Once in a while, when he would beat me on the house shows, he would put his feet on the ropes. For a wrestler, that’s huge, because it gives me an out: ‘You wouldn’t have beaten me if you didn’t put your feet on the ropes; you had to cheat to beat me’. I had a great relationship with the big man. It was a hard life for him. Nowadays, there are a lot of big people, but back then at 7ft4 and 500lbs, it was tough. I was lucky to have what I had with him.”
